historical_reference_context.scope: Historical same-container MI50 e984 versus mx matched measurement. These figures are context beside the new d31/faef screen, never a new matched mx arm or fresh parity claim.

mx.required_recheck: actual F32-KV Vulkan adapter source/hash, linked libraries and --list-devices; do not substitute CPU or default-f16-KV wrapper
mx.linked_library_manifest: .tmp-half-weight-perf-20261002/cpu-initial/mx-reference.json reference_artifacts; reuse only matching GPU build-r2 libraries, not that manifest CPU executable

caveats: Each decode resets history; tg128/32 is not generation after pp64/512.
Historical llmx and mx context allocation/load/arithmetic policies remain those recorded in their original report.
No old rate is subtracted from a new rate to establish a kernel gain, driver effect or occupancy.

screen.monitor_exit_limit: Runner waits for monitor but does not save its return code; no zero inferred.
screen.workload: Same model and LCG histories in both llmx arms. Every pp/tg resets history; tg128/32 is independent of pp64/512. Same model logical context and actual token reach between arms.
limitations: Historical Radeon results are a different environment.
Historical Linux e984/mx matched rows are context only, not a fresh candidate-versus-mx arm or parity proof.
Identical shader modules and actual tile witnesses do not measure occupancy, bandwidth or stalls.
A viable screen needs appropriate later correctness/wider performance qualification; this preparation adds no such runs.
Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; disappeared/new and inaccessible processes are retained as coverage limits. Unavailable GPU counters are not zero.
All calls retained. Positive percentages mean higher candidate throughput; no slow/activity-flagged call is removed.
Two process rates per arm; r1 SD does not measure repeatability. Profile rates are diagnostic only and excluded from comparisons.
Whole-call activity includes loading, warmup and both phases; per-call boundary samples overlap and cannot be summed as unique observations.
New, missed and inaccessible processes are unknown, not idle. GPU ranges have no process attribution.
No occupancy, bandwidth, stall, numerical qualification, same-owner layout-control or fresh mx-parity claim.
